newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Q1 rubber output down 13.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Q1 rubber output down 13.6 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber production fell 13.6 percent to 251,120 tonnes in the first quarter of 1997 from 290,703 tonnes in the year-earlier period, the national Bernama news agency said on Friday.

Export of rubber between January and March this year fell 5.6 percent to 225,854 tonnes from 239,246 tonnes in the same period last year, Bernama quoted the government statistics department as saying.
The United States was the largest buyer of Malaysian rubber, accounting for 12.9 percent of exports. Other major consumers were South Korea, Germany, Belgium, Italy, Britain and China.
Imports of rubber for domestic use grew, coming from Thailand, Liberia, the Philippines, Cambodia, Burma, Vietnam and Cote D'Ivoire.
Imports in the first quarter of 1997 expanded 35.9 percent to 95,199 tonnes from 70,029 tonnes a year ago.
Stocks at the end of March were 220,940 tonnes, up 0.7 percent from last year's 219,490 tonnes.
